reasoning_traces.think:
The file system topology encodes both spatial and temporal semantics. File size entropy (S) provides a measure of information density across the dataset, where H(S) reflects how uniformly distributed file sizes are. This entropy is particularly sensitive to outliers such as .mbox (~13.5 GB) and .zip archives (~9.2 GB), which may indicate batched data ingestion or archival workflows. The data type frequency (N_ext, S_ext) reveals dominant formats like .csv and .zip, suggesting structured data pipelines and compressed assets. Access pattern graphs (A_ij) model inter-file dependencies, enabling prediction of likely next steps in data processing. These primitives form a triadic structure: entropy quantifies disorder, frequency identifies dominant modalities, and graph models causality. Failure modes include overfitting to large files (e.g., .mbox), underrepresentation of small but frequent types (.json, .png), and loss of temporal coherence in access graphs. Dualities emerge between static metadata (size, type) and dynamic usage (access graph).
